Our Services




## Full-Service Residential & Commercial Plumbing Across Texas


From burst pipes at midnight to scheduled water heater replacements, Lone Star Plumbing Co. delivers expert residential plumbing services — and so much more — to homes and businesses throughout our local Texas community. One call gets you a licensed pro who shows up fast and gets it done right.
















### Emergency Plumbing


Burst pipes, flooding, or a sudden loss of water pressure? We're on call 24/7 to respond fast — because plumbing emergencies don't wait for business hours.

Get Emergency Help













### Drain Cleaning


Slow drains and stubborn clogs are no match for our high-pressure hydro-jetting and professional snaking services. We clear it completely — not just temporarily.

Schedule a Cleaning













### Water Heater Repair & Replacement


No hot water is a serious disruption. We repair all makes and models — and install energy-efficient tankless units — to restore comfort quickly and reliably.

Get a Free Estimate













### Leak Detection


Hidden leaks waste water and damage your home silently. Our non-invasive electronic detection pinpoints leaks behind walls and under slabs before they become disasters.

Find My Leak













### Sewer Line Solutions


From camera inspections to trenchless pipe lining and full sewer replacements, we handle the underground issues that cause the biggest headaches — with minimal disruption to your yard.

Inspect My Sewer













### Pre-Sale Plumbing Inspections


Buying or selling a Texas home? Our thorough plumbing inspection report gives buyers peace of mind and helps sellers avoid costly surprises at closing. Trusted by local realtors.

Book an Inspection









Not sure which service you need? Give us a call — we'll walk you through it.

Talk to a Plumber Today

Our Services








# Complete Plumbing Solutions for Texas Homes & Businesses


From burst pipes at midnight to routine maintenance that keeps your systems running strong, Lone Star Plumbing Co. delivers expert residential plumbing services and full-scope commercial solutions across Texas. We show up fast, work clean, and stand behind every job — because your home and livelihood depend on it.














### Residential Plumbing


Built for Texas homeowners who need reliable help fast. Whether it's a clogged drain, a water heater on the fritz, or an emergency leak threatening your property, our licensed plumbers arrive promptly and fix it right the first time. We handle everything from fixture installations and pipe repairs to full remodels and sewer line diagnostics — keeping your household running without disruption.


- Emergency & same-day repairs

- Water heater installation & repair

- Drain cleaning & sewer line service

- Fixture upgrades & remodel support












### Commercial Plumbing


Texas businesses can't afford downtime caused by plumbing failures. Our commercial team handles the full scope of action plumbing — from multi-unit apartment complexes and office buildings to restaurants, retail centers, and industrial facilities. We offer scheduled preventive maintenance programs that protect your infrastructure and keep you compliant, alongside rapid-response service for urgent breakdowns that threaten operations.


- Preventive maintenance contracts

- Backflow prevention & code compliance

- Grease trap & floor drain service

- Multi-unit & new construction plumbing





















Residential Plumbing Services




## What We Handle — Start to Finish


From fast emergency fixes to full residential plumbing services, Lone Star Plumbing Co. brings expert action plumbing, heating, and air solutions to every Texas home we serve.













### Clogged Drains


Slow or fully blocked drains cleared fast using professional-grade snaking and hydro-jetting. We diagnose root cause — not just symptoms.



Same-day response available











### Broken Pipes


Burst or cracked pipes repaired and replaced using durable materials built for Texas temperature swings. We restore water flow and protect your structure.



Long-lasting repair materials











### Slab Leaks


Precision electronic detection locates leaks beneath your foundation without unnecessary demolition. Early detection prevents catastrophic structural damage.



Non-invasive leak detection











### Water Heaters


Installation, repair, and replacement of tank and tankless water heaters. We match the right unit to your household demand and energy goals.



Energy-efficient options available











### Fixture Installation


Faucets, toilets, sinks, showers, and outdoor hose bibs installed cleanly and correctly. Upgrade your home with fixtures that look great and hold up.



Clean install, zero mess left behind











### Sewer Issues


Camera inspections, line clearing, and sewer repair handled by licensed pros. We identify blockages, root intrusions, and collapsed lines before they escalate.



Video camera diagnosis included











### Pressure Problems


Low or dangerously high water pressure diagnosed and corrected. We test PRV valves, supply lines, and municipal connections to restore balanced flow.



Protects pipes and appliances











### Plumbing Inspections


Comprehensive whole-home inspections for buyers, sellers, and homeowners. We document every issue and deliver a clear, code-compliant report.



Full code-confidence reporting
























How It Works

From your first call to final inspection — our residential plumbing services are built around speed, transparency, and quality you can count on.









01

Why Lone Star Plumbing




## Residential Plumbing Services Built for Texas Homes


We know Texas homes — the hard water, the wide temperature swings, the aging infrastructure in established neighborhoods. Lone Star Plumbing Co. combines deep local expertise with the kind of dependable, respectful service that earns referrals from neighbors. Whether it's a routine inspection or a 2 a.m. emergency, we show up ready and we fix it right the first time.


Our team is trained in both modern systems and the older plumbing found across Central Texas, giving us the practical knowledge to deliver long-term fixes — not quick patches that fail again next season.






What Sets Us Apart


- Texas Home Knowledge We understand local water conditions, soil types, and regional building codes — so our fixes are built to last in this climate.

- Dependable Scheduling We respect your time. Appointments are confirmed, technicians arrive on time, and we communicate clearly from booking to completion.

- Emergency Responsiveness Burst pipes and major leaks don't wait. Our emergency line is answered around the clock so you're never left dealing with a crisis alone.

- Respectful In-Home Service Shoe covers, clean work areas, and courteous technicians. We treat your home the way we'd want ours treated — with care and professionalism.

- Practical Long-Term Fixes We diagnose root causes, not symptoms. Every repair is designed to hold up — saving you money and hassle down the road.













Got a plumbing issue — big or small? Our expert team is ready to help with any residential plumbing need across the greater Texas area. Don't wait until a small drip becomes a serious problem.




Get Help Today

Our Story




# Texas-Born, Neighbor-Trusted Plumbing Since Day One


Lone Star Plumbing Co. was built on a simple promise: show up fast, do the job right, and treat every customer like a neighbor — because in Texas, that's exactly what you are. From busted pipes at midnight to whole-home remodels, we deliver residential plumbing services with the kind of hands-on care that big corporate outfits just can't match.


We're locally owned, Texas proud, and personally invested in every job we take on. When you're stressed and your home is on the line, you deserve a plumber who answers the phone, arrives on time, and gets it done. That's the Lone Star standard — and we hold ourselves to it every single day.










### Honesty


Straight talk, fair pricing, and no surprise charges — ever.










### Urgency


We move fast because we know every minute matters in an emergency.










### Craftsmanship


Expert workmanship that lasts — done properly the first time.















































Our Core Values




## Built on Trust. Driven by Pride.


Residential plumbing services done the Texas way — honest, fast, and done right the first time.













### Fast Response


When a pipe bursts or a drain backs up, every minute counts. Lone Star Plumbing Co. dispatches quickly so your home is protected and back to normal without delay. Action plumbing means we show up — day or night.











### Respectful Service


We treat your home like our own. Our technicians arrive in clean uniforms, explain every step clearly, and leave your space tidy. Transparent pricing and no-surprise invoices — because you deserve to be treated right.











### Repairs Done Right


We don't cut corners. Every fix is built to last using quality materials and expert technique. Our work is fully backed — if something isn't right, we make it right. Expert services in plumbing, heating, and beyond, all under one trusted name.











Lone Star Plumbing Co. was built on a simple promise: show up fast, be straight with people, and never leave a job half-done. That's Texas accountability — and it's how we've earned trust in every neighborhood we serve.

Common Questions



## Frequently Asked Questions


Everything you need to know before reaching out. We keep it straight and simple — just like our residential plumbing services.










### How fast do you respond to plumbing emergencies?


We offer 24/7 emergency response across our service area. When a pipe bursts or a drain backs up, we dispatch a licensed technician as quickly as possible — often within the hour. Don't wait; call us the moment something goes wrong.







### What areas does Lone Star Plumbing Co. serve?


We proudly serve homeowners and businesses throughout the greater Texas region. Whether you're in the city or out in the suburbs, our team covers a wide service footprint. Contact us to confirm availability in your specific zip code.







### Do you work on commercial properties too?


Absolutely. We handle both residential and commercial plumbing projects — from single-family homes to multi-unit buildings and small businesses. Our licensed plumbers are equipped for jobs of all sizes and complexity levels.







### What information should I include in my message?


To help us respond quickly and accurately, please include your address or city, a brief description of the issue, and whether it's an emergency. Photos or a short description of what you're seeing go a long way in getting you the right expert fast.







### Are your plumbers licensed and insured?


Yes — every technician on our team is fully licensed, bonded, and insured in the state of Texas. We hold ourselves to the highest standards of action plumbing, heating, and air service so you can trust the work done in your home or business.







### Do you offer free estimates?


For most non-emergency jobs, we're happy to provide a clear, upfront estimate before any work begins. We believe in transparent pricing with no hidden surprises — because trust is the foundation of every job we take on.

# Privacy Policy



Last Updated:  5/18/2026



Lone Star Plumbing Co. ("Company", "we", "our") is committed to protecting your privacy. This privacy policy explains how we collect, use and protect your information when you use our website [business_website] ("Service").


## 1. Information Collection


We may collect the following types of information:


- Personal Information: Name, email address, phone number and address

- Technical Information: IP address, browser type, operating system and website usage data

- Cookies: Information stored on your computer to improve user experience




## 2. Use of Information


We use the collected information for the following purposes:


- Providing requested services

- Improving service and user experience

- Contacting you regarding our services

- Compliance with legal requirements




## 3. Information Sharing


We do not sell, rent or share your personal information with third parties, except in the following cases:


- With your explicit consent

- When required by law

- To protect our rights or user safety

- With service providers who assist in operating the service (under confidentiality agreements)




## 4. User Rights


In accordance with Israeli Privacy Protection Law 1981, you have the following rights:


- Right to access personal information stored about you

- Right to correct inaccurate or incomplete information

- Right to delete personal information in certain circumstances

- Right to object to information processing for marketing purposes

- Right to file a complaint with the Data Protection Authority




## 5. Cookies


Our website uses cookies to improve user experience. You can manage cookies through your browser settings. Disabling cookies may affect website functionality.


## 6. Information Security


We implement reasonable security measures to protect your information, including encryption, firewalls and restricted access control. However, no transmission or storage method is 100% secure.


## 7. Policy Changes


We may update this privacy policy from time to time. Material changes will be posted on the website with 30 days advance notice.



## 8. Contact Information


For questions or requests regarding this privacy policy, please contact us:


- Company: Lone Star Plumbing Co.

- Email: [business_email]

- Phone: [business_phone]

- Address: [business_address]



Data Protection Authority: For complaints, you may contact the Data Protection Authority at the Ministry of Justice

# Accessibility Statement



Last updated:  May 18, 2026



Lone Star Plumbing Co. is committed to making our services accessible to all users. We strive to implement the Israeli Standard (TI 5568) based on WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidelines.


Accessibility Level: AA (Israeli Standard TI 5568)



## 1. Accessibility Policy


We believe in equal rights and the right of every person to receive information and services independently and equally. This website was designed and built with special emphasis on accessibility for people with disabilities.


## 2. Accessibility Arrangements on the Site


- Keyboard navigation support

- Screen reader compatibility

- Appropriate color contrast

- Flexible and scalable font sizes

- Descriptive image alt text

- Hierarchical heading structure

- Clear and descriptive links

- Support for 200% zoom without content loss





### WCAG 2.1 Compliance


The website complies with WCAG 2.1 Level AA, which includes:


- Perceivable: Information is presented in ways users can perceive

- Operable: Interface components are operable

- Understandable: Information and user interface are understandable

- Robust: Content can be interpreted by a variety of technologies





## 3. Supported Assistive Technologies


- NVDA (Windows)

- JAWS (Windows)

- VoiceOver (Mac/iOS)

- TalkBack (Android)

- Dragon NaturallySpeaking

- Switch navigation




## 4. Accessibility Testing


The website has been tested using:


- Automated accessibility testing tools

- Manual testing with screen readers

- Keyboard-only navigation

- Color contrast verification

- Testing with users with disabilities




## 5. Continuous Improvements


We are continuously working to improve the accessibility of our website and update it according to technological developments and user feedback.



## 6. Contact and Feedback


If you encounter an accessibility issue on the site or need assistance, please contact us:


- Company: Lone Star Plumbing Co.

- Email: [business_email]

- Phone: [business_phone]



Response time: We respond to accessibility inquiries within 3 business days and work to resolve issues within 10 business days.

Use of this site constitutes agreement to the terms outlined below. Please read carefully before use.

- "User" - Anyone who browses or uses the site

- "Services" - Home Services / Plumbing provided through the site




## 2. Description of Services


Lone Star Plumbing Co. provides Home Services / Plumbing through the site. The services are subject to the terms detailed in this document and may change from time to time.

## 8. Privacy

## 9. Changes to Terms of Use

## 10. Service Termination


The Company may suspend or limit service at any time, including in cases of terms of use violations. In case of service termination, relevant provisions will remain in effect.


## 11. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution

## 7 Signs You May Have a Hidden Water Leak

Plumbing Tips


# 7 Signs You May Have a Hidden Water Leak




June 12, 2025

·


6 min read

·
By Lone Star Plumbing Co.








Water is one of the most destructive forces in a home — not because of floods or storms, but because of the slow, silent leaks that go undetected for months. A hidden water leak can rot your walls, buckle your floors, spike your utility bills, and invite dangerous mold growth before you ever notice a single drip. In Texas, where homes face both scorching summers and surprise cold snaps, your plumbing takes a beating year-round.


The good news? Your home usually tells you something is wrong — if you know what to look for. Here are seven warning signs that you may have a hidden water leak somewhere in your plumbing system.


## 1. Your Water Bill Has Spiked Without Explanation


If your monthly water bill has jumped noticeably and your household habits haven't changed, that extra water is going somewhere. A slow, steady leak from a pipe inside your walls or under your slab can waste thousands of gallons per month. Pull out your last three to six months of bills and look for an upward trend that doesn't match the season or your usage.


## 2. You Hear Running Water When Nothing Is On


Walk through your home at night when everything is quiet. If you can hear water moving — a faint hiss, a trickle, or a subtle rushing sound — behind walls, under floors, or near the water heater, take it seriously. That sound is water escaping where it shouldn't be. This is one of the clearest early signals of a slab leak or a pressurized pipe failure.


## 3. Warm or Hot Spots on Your Floor


Feel unusually warm patches on your tile or hardwood floor? A hot water line running beneath your concrete slab may be leaking. The heat from the escaping hot water transfers directly through the slab and into your flooring. This is a classic sign of a slab leak and requires immediate professional attention before structural damage sets in.


## 4. Visible Mold, Mildew, or Musty Odors


Mold thrives in moisture-rich environments. If you notice dark spots on walls, ceilings, or baseboards — especially in bathrooms, laundry rooms, or along exterior walls — moisture is accumulating behind the surface. Even without visible mold, a persistent musty or earthy smell in a room that should be dry is a strong indicator of hidden moisture from a leak nearby.


## 5. Stained, Warped, or Bubbling Walls and Ceilings


Water stains that appear as yellow or brown rings on your ceiling or walls are a telltale sign. So is paint that is bubbling, peeling, or blistering without a clear cause. Drywall that feels soft or spongy to the touch has absorbed water — and that water had to come from somewhere. Don't assume it was a one-time event; treat it as an active leak until proven otherwise.


## 6. Your Water Meter Keeps Moving When You're Not Using Water


Here's a simple test every Texas homeowner should know: turn off every faucet, appliance, and water-using device in your home. Then go outside and watch your water meter for 15 minutes. If the dial or digital display is still moving, water is flowing through your system — and it's going somewhere unintended. This is one of the most reliable DIY methods for detecting a hidden water leak before calling a plumber.


## 7. Lush, Unusually Green Patches in Your Yard


If one section of your lawn is dramatically greener, thicker, or faster-growing than the rest — even during a dry spell — you may have an underground pipe leak beneath your yard. The escaping water acts as a constant irrigation source for the grass above it. Similarly, soft or soggy ground in a dry climate with no recent rainfall is a strong sign of a buried pipe failure.


## What to Do If You Spot These Signs


Don't wait. Hidden water leaks get worse over time, and the longer they go unaddressed, the more expensive the repair becomes. At Lone Star Plumbing Co., our licensed Texas plumbers use advanced leak detection equipment to pinpoint the exact location of a leak without unnecessary damage to your home. Whether it's a slab leak, a pinhole pipe, or a slow drip behind your drywall, we'll find it fast and fix it right.


If you've noticed any of these signs in your home, give us a call today. We serve homeowners across the greater Texas area with same-day and emergency plumbing services — because when it comes to water damage, every hour counts.

Plumbing Tips


# How to Prevent Frozen Pipes During Sudden Texas Cold Snaps




January 14, 2025

·


6 min read

·
By Lone Star Plumbing Co.








Most Texans don't think much about frozen pipes — and that's exactly the problem. Unlike homeowners in Minnesota or Colorado who winterize every fall without a second thought, Texans are often caught off guard when a sudden Arctic blast pushes temperatures below freezing for days at a time. The result? Burst pipes, flooded homes, and emergency calls flooding our phone lines. We've seen it firsthand after every major freeze event, and we want to help you stay ahead of it.


The good news is that preventing frozen pipes doesn't require expensive upgrades or a full plumbing overhaul. A few smart habits and targeted preparations can save you thousands of dollars in water damage repairs. Here's what every Texas homeowner should know before the next cold snap hits.


## Why Texas Pipes Are Especially Vulnerable


Homes built in warmer climates are designed with heat efficiency in mind, not cold resilience. That means pipes are often routed through uninsulated exterior walls, attic spaces, garages, and crawl spaces — areas that plunge rapidly when temperatures drop. Unlike northern states where building codes require insulated pipe runs, Texas construction standards have historically assumed mild winters. The 2021 freeze was a stark reminder of just how exposed our infrastructure really is.


When water freezes inside a pipe, it expands with enormous force — enough to crack copper, split PVC, and blow apart fittings. The real damage often doesn't appear until the pipe thaws and water rushes out of the breach. By then, ceilings, walls, and flooring can absorb hundreds of gallons before anyone notices.


## Step 1: Insulate Exposed Pipes Before the Freeze Arrives


Foam pipe insulation sleeves are inexpensive, easy to install, and available at any hardware store. Focus on pipes in unheated areas: under sinks on exterior walls, in the garage, in the attic, and along any exterior wall cavity. Wrap outdoor hose bibs with insulated covers — these are the first points to freeze and one of the most common sources of burst pipes.


For pipes in especially exposed locations, consider adding electric heat tape. This self-regulating tape wraps around the pipe and activates when temperatures approach freezing. It's a worthwhile investment for any pipe that runs through an unheated garage or a drafty crawl space.


## Step 2: Keep a Slow Drip Running on Vulnerable Faucets


Running water is much harder to freeze than standing water. On nights when temperatures are expected to drop below 28°F — especially for extended periods — let your most vulnerable faucets drip slowly. Prioritize faucets on exterior walls and those fed by pipes that run through unheated spaces. Even a thin trickle of cold water keeps pressure moving and dramatically reduces freeze risk.


Don't forget to disconnect and drain garden hoses before a freeze. A connected hose traps water in the bib and the supply line behind it, creating a freeze point right at the wall. This is one of the simplest and most overlooked prevention steps.


## Step 3: Maintain Indoor Heat — Even When You're Away


If you're leaving town during a cold snap, resist the urge to turn the thermostat down to 55°F to save on your energy bill. Keep your home at a minimum of 65°F. The few extra dollars in heating costs are nothing compared to the cost of emergency pipe repair and water damage restoration. Open cabinet doors under sinks on exterior walls to allow warm air to circulate around the pipes.


If your home has a crawl space, make sure vents are closed during a freeze. In warmer months, open crawl space vents promote airflow and prevent moisture buildup — but in a freeze, they let frigid air flow directly over uninsulated pipes below your floor.


## Step 4: Know Where Your Main Shutoff Is


Even with every precaution in place, pipes can still freeze and burst. Knowing how to shut off your main water supply immediately can be the difference between a manageable repair and a catastrophic flood. Locate your main shutoff valve now — before you need it. In most Texas homes, it's near the water meter at the street or inside the home near the water heater. Make sure every adult in your household knows where it is and how to use it.


If you suspect a pipe has frozen but hasn't burst yet, turn off the main water supply and call a licensed plumber before attempting to thaw it yourself. Improper thawing — especially with open flame — can cause immediate pipe failure or even a fire. Our team at Lone Star Plumbing Co. is available around the clock for exactly these situations.


## When to Call a Professional


If you notice reduced water pressure, no water from a faucet, visible frost on exposed pipes, or wet spots on walls or ceilings after a freeze, call a licensed plumber immediately. These are signs that a pipe may have already frozen or burst. Acting fast limits the damage and gets your home back to normal faster.


Frozen pipe prevention is one of the most cost-effective things a Texas homeowner can do. A few hours of preparation before a cold snap can protect your home from thousands of dollars in damage. If you have questions about winterizing your plumbing or want a professional inspection before the next freeze, give Lone Star Plumbing Co. a call. We're your local experts — and we show up when it matters most.

Plumbing Tips


# What Not to Put Down Your Garbage Disposal




June 12, 2025

•


5 min read

•
By Lone Star Plumbing Co.







Your garbage disposal is one of the most convenient appliances in your kitchen — until it isn't. A jammed, clogged, or burned-out disposal can turn a simple dinner cleanup into a plumbing emergency. The good news? Most disposal problems are completely preventable. Knowing what not to put down your garbage disposal is the single best thing you can do to protect this hardworking appliance and the drain lines behind it.


At Lone Star Plumbing Co., we get called out for disposal issues regularly — and almost every time, the culprit is something that should never have gone down the drain in the first place. Here's the definitive list of what to keep out of your disposal, and why it matters.


## Grease, Fats, and Cooking Oils


This is the number one offender. Grease might pour down in liquid form when it's hot, but it cools and solidifies inside your pipes — coating the walls and trapping food debris over time. Even if your disposal handles it fine, the drain line behind it won't. You'll end up with a stubborn blockage that often requires professional hydro-jetting to clear. Instead, pour cooled grease into an old can or jar and toss it in the trash.


## Fibrous Vegetables


Celery, asparagus, artichokes, onion skins, and corn husks are all fibrous — and those stringy fibers wrap around your disposal's impeller blades like a tourniquet. The motor strains, the blades jam, and you're left with a disposal that hums but won't spin. Peel and trim fibrous vegetables over the trash can, not the sink.


## Eggshells


There's a persistent myth that eggshells sharpen disposal blades. They don't — and the thin membrane inside the shell can wrap around the grinding components just like fibrous material. The crushed shell particles also combine with grease in pipes to form a thick, sandy paste. Compost your eggshells or toss them in the trash.


## Coffee Grounds


Coffee grounds feel harmless going down — they're small, they smell fine, and the water seems to flush them away easily. But grounds accumulate in the trap and drain line, building up into a thick, dense sludge. Over time, this is a recipe for a slow drain that turns into a full clog. Compost grounds or dispose of them in the garbage.


## Pasta, Rice, and Starchy Foods


Starchy foods expand when they absorb water. Cooked pasta and rice will keep swelling inside your drain lines and disposal trap long after they've gone down. The resulting paste-like blockage is tough to break up and can trap other debris. Scrape plates into the trash before rinsing them at the sink.


## Bones and Hard Food Scraps


Chicken bones, fruit pits, popcorn kernels, and nut shells are simply too hard for a standard residential garbage disposal to handle. These items will spin around the grinding chamber repeatedly, dulling the impellers and potentially cracking the disposal housing. Small fish bones are usually okay, but when in doubt, throw it out.


## Potato Peels


Potato peels are a silent disposal killer. They pass through the blades easily, but the starchy pulp they create coats the inside of your pipes and forms a thick, sticky film. A large batch of peels can cause an immediate clog. Peel potatoes over a bowl or the trash can — your disposal will thank you.


## Non-Food Items


It sounds obvious, but disposals get used as catch-alls more often than you'd think. Twist ties, rubber bands, glass shards, bottle caps, paper, and cigarette butts have all been found in disposals we've serviced. These items cause immediate mechanical damage and can void your warranty. Keep a strainer basket over the drain when the disposal isn't actively in use.


## When to Call a Professional


If your disposal is humming without spinning, leaking from the bottom, tripping its reset button repeatedly, or simply won't turn on — it's time to call a plumber. Some issues like a simple jam can be resolved with the hex key tool under the unit, but persistent problems usually signal a worn motor, damaged seals, or a blockage deeper in the drain line that needs professional attention.


Lone Star Plumbing Co. serves homeowners across Texas with fast, honest disposal repair and replacement. Whether you need a quick fix or a full unit swap, our licensed plumbers show up on time and get the job done right. Give us a call before a small disposal problem turns into a bigger plumbing headache.

Plumbing Tips


# When a Running Toilet Is More Than a Minor Annoyance




June 12, 2025

·


5 min read

·
By Lone Star Plumbing Co.








That faint hiss coming from your bathroom at 2 a.m. might not seem like a big deal. You jiggle the handle, the sound stops, and you head back to bed. But here in Texas, where water bills already climb during the long, dry summers, a running toilet is quietly costing you real money — and it may be signaling a bigger problem lurking inside your tank.


## How Much Water Does a Running Toilet Actually Waste?


A toilet that runs continuously can waste anywhere from 200 to over 1,000 gallons of water per day, depending on the severity of the leak. At average Texas water rates, that translates to an extra $30 to $70 on your monthly utility bill — sometimes more. Over the course of a year, a single leaking toilet can cost a household hundreds of dollars in wasted water. If you've noticed your bill creeping upward without an obvious explanation, your toilet is one of the first places we check.


## The Most Common Causes Behind a Running Toilet


Most running toilet problems trace back to one of three components inside the tank:


The flapper valve is a rubber seal at the bottom of the tank. Over time, it warps, hardens, or accumulates mineral deposits — especially common in areas with hard water like much of Central Texas. When the flapper doesn't seal completely, water trickles continuously from the tank into the bowl, forcing the fill valve to keep running to compensate.


The fill valve itself can also wear out or become misadjusted. If the float is set too high, water spills into the overflow tube and drains away silently. You may never hear it, but it runs around the clock.


The flush handle and chain are simpler culprits — a chain that's too short, tangled, or caught under the flapper prevents a proper seal after every flush. This is often the easiest fix, but it's also easy to overlook.


## When It's More Than a DIY Fix


Replacing a flapper or adjusting a float arm is a reasonable weekend project for a handy homeowner. But if you've already swapped the flapper and the toilet is still running, the problem may run deeper. Cracks in the overflow tube, a failing fill valve assembly, or even a hairline fracture in the porcelain can all cause persistent running. In older homes, corroded shut-off valves behind the toilet can also complicate any repair — attempting to turn them off can cause them to fail entirely, turning a minor fix into an urgent situation.


That's when it's time to call a licensed plumber. At Lone Star Plumbing Co., our technicians carry the parts and tools to diagnose and resolve toilet issues on the first visit. We don't just fix the symptom — we inspect the full toilet system to make sure nothing else is about to give way.


## The Hidden Risk: Water Damage


A running toilet that goes unaddressed long enough can do more than inflate your water bill. Constant moisture around the base of the toilet — sometimes caused by a faulty wax ring that a running toilet can accelerate — leads to subfloor rot, mold growth, and tile damage. What starts as a $15 flapper replacement can quietly become a $1,500 subfloor repair if left too long. Texas summers don't help: the combination of heat and humidity creates ideal conditions for mold to take hold fast once moisture gets into the floor structure.


## What You Can Do Right Now


Start with the dye test: drop a few food coloring drops into your toilet tank and wait 15 minutes without flushing. If color appears in the bowl, water is leaking past the flapper. That's your confirmation that something needs attention. From there, assess whether it's a quick part swap or something that warrants a professional eye. When in doubt, a same-day service call from Lone Star Plumbing Co. will give you a clear answer — and peace of mind — fast.


Don't let a small drip drain your budget. Give us a call and we'll take care of it the right way, the first time.
